definition: Law and motion calendar is a court’s or a specific judge’s schedule for when and what types of motions and legal arguments will be heard. The law and motion calendar allocates an appropriate amount of time to hear the motions and arguments during a given hour, day, week, etc. These calendars are focused on hearing pretrial motions as well as other legal arguments or requests that do not constitute part of a trial. For example, a motion to compel an answer to a discovery request is a matter that could appear on a judge’s law and motion calendar. Not all motions appear on the calendar. Whether a motion appears on the law and motion calendar depends on the applicable court rules, and in some jurisdictions, the practices of the individual judge. Some motions may be decided without oral argument or handled through a separate procedure. lateral support / law and motion calendar Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
